title: Reading Between the Vague Lines

fn.en: Recognize vague language in listening; use compound adjectives.

gr: compound adjectives, and the vague language that surrounds them

items.q: Hipsters reject ___ culture.
Do you listen to ___ bands nobody else has heard of?
Hipsters have a taste for little-___ bands.
Zátopek was ___ for his hard training routines.

tts: Every era has a social group that rebels against society in some way. In the sixties it was hippies, in the seventies punks, in the eighties goths. Now the latest subculture is the hipster.

Hipsters are young people, in their twenties and thirties usually, who reject mainstream culture. They are kind of anti anything that is popular — art, music, clothes and so on. They tend to be well educated, and many of them work in creative fields like media or publishing, that sort of thing.

Your stereotypical hipster wears tight-fitting jeans and large thick-rimmed glasses, whether they need them or not. They wear old-fashioned retro-style shirts with checked or flowery patterns, often bought from vintage or second-hand shops. You rarely see a clean-shaven male hipster.
But what I should explain is that hipsters do not actually want to be labelled as hipsters. They do not want to be part of a group; they want to be seen as individuals.

items.q: What is a hipster, according to the speaker?
o: A young person who rejects mainstream culture

items.q: What is the paradox she points out?
o: Hipsters do not want to be labelled as hipsters
They are all the same age

items.q: Where do their clothes usually come from?

tts: There are hipster neighbourhoods in many major cities, full of trendy cafés, galleries, second-hand shops and so on. They tend to be districts that are historically poor and run-down but are now fashionable places to live and work.

As for music, all sorts of bands really, as long as they are obscure and nobody else has heard of them. Hipsters are very critical of mainstream music and of those who like it. The same with film, books and art. That is why hipsters are not very popular: they think their tastes are superior to others.

They are anti-consumerism, which is why they buy second-hand things and believe in mending things when they break rather than always buying something new. They are also very green, so they buy eco-friendly products.
The ultimate cool hipster accessory is the fixed-wheel bike, or fixie. They are sort of like modern versions of retro-style bikes with just one gear.
Hipsters are keen on old-fashioned pastimes like knitting, woodwork, growing your own vegetables, making home-made jam, baking cakes and stuff like that.

items.s: Hipster neighbourhoods tend to be historically poor districts.
They like bands that everybody has heard of.
They prefer mending things to buying new ones.
Knitting and woodwork are described as typical hipster pastimes.

items.q: “a sort of orange colour” — why does the speaker say sort of?
o: She cannot find a precise word for it
She is uncertain whether it exists

items.q: “laptops, shopping bags or whatever” — what does or whatever do?
o: Signals that the list could continue

items.q: “music and stuff like that” — what kind of expression is this?
Why is vague language so common in speech?
o: Speakers do not have time to find the exact word, and precision is often unnecessary

acts.title: Compound adjectives, and being vague on purpose
rule: Two things sit together in this lesson because they do the same job from opposite directions. A compound adjective packs a whole description into one hyphenated word. Vague language does the reverse: it leaves the description open because the exact word is not worth the time.
points: thick-rimmed glasses, floral-patterned dresses, long-haired, blue-eyed.
home-made jam, second-hand shops, hand-written letters.
Compound adjectives take a hyphen before the noun: a well-known band. After the verb, usually not: the band is well known.
kind of / sort of when you cannot find the word; and so on, or whatever, and stuff like that when the list could continue.
eg: It’s a sort of orange colour.
records, cameras and stuff like that
acts.careful: “a well known band” before the noun and “the band is well-known” after the verb are both wrong. The hyphen goes in only when the compound sits in front of what it describes.

write.q: Describe a subculture or a recognizable group where you live — how they dress, what they own, where they go. Write about 180 words. Use at least six compound adjectives with correct hyphens, and at least three vague expressions, placed where a precise word would sound absurd.
write.model:
There is a group in the cafés round the university who would be recognized anywhere, and who would deny being a group at all.

You would know them by the coat: a long, second-hand, slightly-too-large wool thing from a vintage shop on Erzhanov, worn over tight-fitting jeans and heavy thick-soled boots. Half of them wear thick-rimmed glasses. Most of the men have the beard, and the ones who do not look self-conscious about it.

What they own is deliberately low-tech — a film camera, a record player, a fixed-wheel bike or whatever the current version is. What they reject is anything that has become popular, which includes several bands they liked eighteen months ago.

The paradox is the same one that has applied to every such group since the sixties. They dress in order not to be labelled, and the result is that you can identify them from forty metres, in the dark, and stuff like that.
